Working notes:

- Order form v1 requires fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Source aliases map as follows:
  - customer -> cust
  - quantity -> qty
  - priority/prio -> priority
  - country/shipping country likely -> ship_country
- Validate every required field explicitly before submission. A record can be rejected for multiple missing/invalid fields, then for a remaining single field.
- Do not assume remarks such as “ordinary priority,” “duplicate check done,” or “customer confirmed” satisfy required fields; the structured source must contain valid values.
- On retries, retain already-valid data and correct all reported invalid fields, especially priority and ship_country.
- Three failed attempts send the record to manual review; avoid wasting attempts on partial fixes.
- Successful examples (ORD-5101, ORD-5103, ORD-5108) were accepted on attempt 2 after correcting initial priority and ship_country issues.
- ORD-5104–ORD-5106 demonstrate that fixing priority alone is insufficient when ship_country remains invalid; check the complete required-field set each time.
- Duplicate status does not affect field validation.

Working notes:

- Order forms v1–v3 require the same fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Source aliases:
  - customer -> cust
  - quantity -> qty
  - priority/prio -> priority
  - country/shipping country -> ship_country
- Validate every required field explicitly before submission. Check the full set on every retry; a record may have multiple invalid fields.
- Structured values are required. Do not treat remarks such as “ordinary priority,” “customer confirmed,” “duplicate check done,” or “new” as field values.
- Preserve valid data across retries, but correct every reported invalid field. In particular, fixing priority alone does not resolve an invalid ship_country; fixing priority and ship_country may still require correcting qty.
- Versions 2 and 3 retain the same required-field set and validation behavior as v1.
- Three failed attempts send the record to manual review. Avoid partial fixes that waste attempts.
- Recent failures (ORD-5110–ORD-5118) repeatedly involved invalid priority and/or ship_country, with qty also invalid in ORD-5110–ORD-5111. Repeatedly resubmitting without a complete correction leads to manual review.
- ORD-5119 was accepted on attempt 2 after correction, confirming that handwritten/transcribed source data can pass when all structured fields are valid.
- Duplicate status and confirmation-email requests do not affect field validation.

Working notes:

- Order forms v1–v4 require the same fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Versions 2–4 show the same validation behavior as v1.
- Source aliases:
  - customer -> cust
  - quantity -> qty
  - priority/prio -> priority
  - country/shipping country -> ship_country
- Validate every required field explicitly before submission. Recheck the complete set on every retry; multiple fields may be invalid.
- Structured values are required. Do not use remarks such as “ordinary priority,” “customer confirmed,” “duplicate check done,” or “new” as field values.
- Preserve valid data across retries, but correct all reported invalid fields. Fixing priority alone may leave ship_country or qty invalid; partial fixes waste attempts.
- Three failed attempts send the record to manual review. Submit only after confirming every field is valid.
- Recent failures ORD-5110–ORD-5123 and ORD-5125–ORD-5129 repeatedly involved invalid priority, qty, and/or ship_country. ORD-5120–5122 and ORD-5125–5127 reached manual review after incomplete corrections.
- ORD-5119 and ORD-5124 were accepted after correction, confirming that handwritten/transcribed or portal source data can pass when all structured fields are valid.
- Version 4 adds no new required fields or validation rules.
- Duplicate status, confirmation-email requests, and intake comments do not affect field validation.

Working notes:

- Order forms v1–v5 require the same six fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Version 5 has shown no additional fields or rules.
- Source aliases:
  - customer -> cust
  - quantity -> qty
  - priority/prio -> priority
  - country/shipping country -> ship_country
- Validate every required field explicitly before submission. On every retry, recheck the complete set; multiple fields may remain invalid after a correction.
- Structured values are mandatory. Do not use intake comments such as “ordinary priority,” “customer confirmed,” “duplicate check done,” “new,” or “confirmation email” as field values.
- Preserve valid data across retries, but correct every reported invalid field. Priority, qty, and ship_country remain frequent failure points.
- Three failed attempts send the record to manual review. Submit only after confirming all six fields are valid.
- ORD-5130 and ORD-5133 reached manual review with incomplete corrections; ORD-5136–5138 similarly show that changing qty alone does not resolve invalid priority/ship_country. ORD-5139 again had invalid qty and ship_country.
- ORD-5135 was accepted after correction, confirming that version 5 and intake comments about “ordinary priority” do not alter validation; acceptance depends on structured fields.
- Handwritten/transcribed, portal, phone-confirmed, duplicate-check, and confirmation-email contexts do not change validation.

Working notes:

- Versions 1–6 list the same six fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Version 6 has not changed validation requirements.
- Version 7 lists cust, destination, email, order_date, priority, qty, but validation still reported ship_country as invalid. Treat destination as an additional/renamed field while retaining canonical ship_country unless validation clearly confirms otherwise; verify both when version 7 appears.
- Source aliases:
  - customer -> cust
  - quantity -> qty
  - priority/prio -> priority
  - country/shipping country -> ship_country
  - destination is not yet proven equivalent to ship_country.
- Validate every required field explicitly before submission. On every retry, recheck the complete set; multiple fields may remain invalid after a correction.
- Use structured values only. Intake comments such as “ordinary priority,” “customer confirmed,” “duplicate check done,” “new,” or “confirmation email” are not field values and do not alter validation.
- Preserve valid data across retries, but correct every reported invalid field. Priority, qty, ship_country, and now destination are frequent failure points.
- Three failed attempts send the record to manual review. Submit only after confirming all applicable fields are valid.
- ORD-5140–5142 confirm that comments, partner-portal intake, and version 6 do not change validation. ORD-5143 and ORD-5145 were accepted after correcting all reported fields.
- ORD-5146–5148 show that changing qty or priority alone is insufficient; destination and legacy ship_country may both need correction under version 7. ORD-5149 again failed on destination, priority, and ship_country.
- Handwritten/transcribed, portal, phone-confirmed, and confirmation-email contexts do not change validation.

Working notes:

- Versions 1–6 require: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Version 7 displays cust, destination, email, order_date, priority, qty, but validation still requires legacy ship_country too.
- Source aliases:
  - customer → cust
  - quantity → qty
  - priority/prio → priority
  - country/shipping country → ship_country
  - destination is a separate version-7 field, not a replacement for ship_country.
- Under version 7, destination must use a valid country code (e.g., DE, FR, ES), not the full country name. The country-name forms were rejected; coded destination values passed destination validation.
- Continue supplying and validating both destination and ship_country. ship_country remains invalid even when destination is corrected, so provide it explicitly in the expected structured format (likely the same country code); do not assume destination populates it.
- Validate every required field explicitly before submission. On every retry, recheck the complete set; multiple fields may remain invalid after a correction.
- Use structured values only. Comments such as “ordinary priority,” “customer confirmed,” “duplicate check done,” “new,” or “confirmation email,” and intake channels do not affect validation.
- Preserve valid data across retries, but correct every reported invalid field. Priority remains a frequent failure point; confirm its exact allowed structured value rather than relying on prose.
- Three failed attempts send the record to manual review. Submit only after all applicable fields are valid.
- ORD-5150–5159 reinforce that version 7 commonly fails destination, priority, and ship_country. Correcting destination alone is insufficient; ORD-5159 shows coded destination can pass while ship_country remains invalid.
